5.description: Comprehensive enterprise-grade capability with strong implementation and extensive supporting evidence.

4.description: Strong capability with only minor limitations or missing advanced features.

3.description: Meets core enterprise requirements but lacks several advanced capabilities.

2.description: Partial implementation with significant functional limitations.

1.description: Minimal capability or no meaningful support for the evaluated criterion.

not_evaluated.description: Insufficient publicly available evidence to make a defensible assessment.

High.description: Multiple high-quality, authoritative sources consistently support the assigned score.

Medium.description: Adequate supporting evidence exists, but coverage or consistency is limited.

Low.description: Limited publicly available evidence; the assigned score should be interpreted with caution.

High / Medium.description: Evidence contains a combination of high- and medium-confidence supporting sources.

Medium / Low.description: Evidence contains a combination of medium- and low-confidence supporting sources.

scoring_principles: Scores must be based on demonstrated capabilities rather than unsupported assumptions.
Evidence confidence does not directly modify the numerical score.
The same scoring standard must be applied consistently across all vendors.
A criterion with insufficient evidence must be marked Not Evaluated rather than assigned an estimated score.
Score justification must explain the evidence-based reasoning behind the assigned score.
Scores must remain traceable to the supporting evidence sources.
